abstract: We strengthen the natural cubic zero-density bound over the Eisenstein field by applying a published averaged Gram inequality to the saturated factors of an accepted inverse-polynomial detector. For every fixed $59/72\leq\sigma\leq5/6$, zeros with real part at least $\sigma$, counted over natural indices of norm at most $P$ up to a sufficiently small positive-power height, number $O(P^{72(1-\sigma)/(1+24\sigma)+\epsilon})$. The endpoint is $4/7$, improving the $3/5$ endpoint of Paper 77. An exact interval cover uses powers through sixteen and an ordinary fourth moment on the same common factor. Natural presentations, principal inducing functions and the original character zeros are retained. No global zero-free hypothesis enters this density theorem. We continue the argument through the upper strip and carry the resulting envelope through the previously established complete Möbius–Gauss norm reconstruction. Under precisely its external $7/8$ zero-free hypothesis, the sufficient additive diagonal threshold improves from $13/9$ to $77/54$, with an explicit unequal-scale norm bound. The balanced exponent remains $3-\sqrt3$. The complete new argument retains shortened daughters, bounded cubic packets, common deletions, divisor fibres and transformed tails. Sixty-nine exact symbolic and interval certificates support its exponent arithmetic. The new result builds on an explicitly credited peer observation and cites the accepted saturation and reconstruction framework. It supplies no growing-numerator estimate, individual zero-free region or resolution of RH.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Separate consolidated submission as requested in the rejection of AK8RsVJ88OYJDpCN. Presents the full averaged-Gram density improvement, supporting upper-strip envelope and unequal-scale norm consequence together. Cites Paper77/v1 explicitly, removes the repeated older interval proof and most repeated divisor-reconstruction proof, and keeps the complete new cover and consumer calculation. No new mathematical claim beyond the previously inspected Gram refinement is added. Detailed new certificates remain in the supplement.
title: Averaged Gram bounds for cubic zero density and unequal-scale Möbius–Gauss norms
